definition: Stage describes the dominant commercial uncertainty and work required, not employee count or a universal timeline.

rules: Evidence outranks self-declared stage; disagreement remains visible.
Unknown evidence does not mean the business failed a stage.
Assign per material business model or segment when one company contains several stages.
Manual override requires reason, reviewer and expiry; it does not create missing evidence.

stages.name: Idea
stages.definition: A candidate opportunity exists, with customer, problem and value claims still largely untested.
entry_criteria: An opportunity or technology hypothesis is named; no external validation is presumed.
exit_criteria: One initial customer/problem hypothesis and its riskiest assumption are explicit.
A feasible, permitted route to contact relevant customers is identified.
primary_risks: Building for a nonexistent or low-priority problem
primary_management_priorities: Choose an initial segment and learning objective
anti_patterns: Treating a market-size slide as demand proof
Using funding or company age to assign stage
recommended_actions: Write a dated hypothesis and list alternative explanations
Choose a low-cost learning test before a feature roadmap
goals: Turn an idea into a falsifiable problem/customer hypothesis
experiments: Interview recruitment smoke test; success means reaching relevant people, not proving demand
decisions: Investigate, reframe or stop this opportunity
completion_criteria: Initial segment, circumstances and uncertainty are recorded, including unknowns.
next_stage_criteria: Customer access exists and a discovery plan addresses the highest uncertainty.
deferred: ROIC and LTV calculations without meaningful operating history
blocking_data: Target customer or access route missing for discovery recruitment

stages.name: Discovery
stages.definition: Customer circumstances, existing alternatives and the significance of the problem are being investigated.
entry_criteria: A target segment and interview/research access route are explicit.
exit_criteria: Traceable observations support a recurring problem in a defined context, with contradictory cases retained.
A proposed value hypothesis and experiment are justified by the observations.
primary_risks: Generalizing from friends or a single anecdote
anti_patterns: Counting interviews as proof of demand
Asking hypothetical willingness-to-pay questions as decisive proof
recommended_actions: Research how a recent problem was handled
goals: Understand whose problem matters and why current alternatives fail
experiments: Concierge walkthrough of a proposed outcome without implying a finished product
decisions: Test solution value or return to idea
completion_criteria: Problem claims have source-linked observations and explicit limitations.
next_stage_criteria: A solution hypothesis can be tested safely with a relevant segment and predeclared evidence criteria.
blocking_data: No credible observations about a problem for the selected segment

stages.name: Validation
stages.definition: Experiments test whether a proposed offer creates useful outcomes and whether customers will make meaningful commitments.
entry_criteria: Problem evidence and a testable solution/value hypothesis exist.
exit_criteria: A relevant customer can obtain the intended value through an MVP or permitted prototype.
Commitment evidence and delivery feasibility are reviewed against predeclared context-specific criteria.
typical_problems: Building a comprehensive product before testing its key assumption
primary_risks: False positives from subsidies or founder relationships
Prototype outcomes that cannot be delivered economically
primary_management_priorities: Test value, price and delivery assumptions
Instrument the first meaningful outcome and preserve test limitations
anti_patterns: Changing the success threshold after seeing results
recommended_actions: Run a small, safe MVP/concierge/pilot test
Distinguish usage, non-binding intent, binding commitment and collected cash
goals: Test problem–solution fit and business-model assumptions
experiments: Price/offer test with an explicit commitment action
Technical/operational feasibility test when delivery is uncertain
decisions: Persevere, pivot, retest inconclusive evidence or stop
Choose the smallest next delivery commitment
completion_criteria: Test observations, interpretation and action are recorded separately.
Failed and inconclusive tests remain visible.
next_stage_criteria: Initial customers actually receive value and return/renewal or repeatable adoption can now be observed.
optional: A/B testing when traffic and identification support it
blocking_data: No value-delivery or customer-commitment observations for the key hypothesis
non_blocking_data: Statistically powered A/B result when a safer qualitative/behavioral test is appropriate

stages.name: Early traction
stages.definition: Real customers use or buy the offer; repeatability, retention, value and economics remain uncertain.
entry_criteria: Documented customers have received the intended outcome.
exit_criteria: Retention/renewal or business-model-appropriate repeatability evidence is reviewed by segment/cohort.
Acquisition and delivery economics and cash requirements have credible observed inputs.
A bounded growth test has explicit guardrails.
typical_problems: Aggregate sign-up growth conceals weak value
Heavy manual effort is omitted from costs
primary_risks: Cohorts are too recent to reveal failure or renewal
primary_management_priorities: Measure relevant cohorts and economic drivers
anti_patterns: Using funding rounds or headcount as proof
Demanding repeated purchase from a naturally one-off product
recommended_actions: Review retained value, losses and customer reasons together
Run limited acquisition tests while investigating weak retention
goals: Assess segment-specific PMF evidence and repeatable delivery
experiments: Bounded channel test with spending limit
decisions: Continue learning, refine segment, or authorize a bounded growth test
Assess PMF as supported/contradicted/unknown for a named segment
completion_criteria: Observed repeatability and limitations are documented, including cohort age.
next_stage_criteria: Context-specific demand/value and economics evidence justify controlled growth; no universal benchmark is applied.
deferred: Broad geographic rollout before local assumptions are tested
blocking_data: Retention or equivalent repeatability evidence missing when material acquisition expansion is requested
Cash exposure unknown before spending commitment
non_blocking_data: Stable LTV when cohorts are immature

stages.name: Growth
stages.definition: The company is testing and improving a repeatable acquisition and delivery engine in validated segments.
entry_criteria: A reviewed evidence case supports controlled expansion in a named segment.
exit_criteria: Multiple measured growth cycles preserve customer outcomes and economic guardrails.
Capacity, cash and management constraints for broader replication are explicit.
primary_risks: Evidence from one segment is applied to another
primary_management_priorities: Test incremental rather than only blended economics
Coordinate growth with cash and delivery constraints
anti_patterns: Assuming historical LTV persists after changing channel or segment
recommended_actions: Release growth spending in bounded increments
Monitor new-cohort quality and cash scenarios together
goals: Expand a proven segment while preserving sustainable value delivery
experiments: Capacity stress pilot within safe service limits
decisions: Expand, hold or reduce a channel
Invest in capacity or revisit value proposition
completion_criteria: Growth case includes customer value, incremental economics, cash and operational constraints.
next_stage_criteria: The operating model can be replicated with defined accountabilities and monitored guardrails.
optional: New product/region exploration as a separate discovery branch
deferred: Assuming every business must pursue venture-scale expansion
blocking_data: Marginal acquisition/fulfillment costs or material cash constraints unknown for the proposed expansion

stages.name: Scale
stages.definition: A repeatable operating model is being replicated across greater volume, units or markets with explicit governance and adaptation.
entry_criteria: Repeated growth evidence and operating constraints support a specified replication plan.
exit_criteria: No universal terminal completion; review whether each replication meets its own customer, economic and control criteria.
primary_management_priorities: Preserve feedback and challenge assumptions in new contexts
anti_patterns: Copying a playbook to new geography without validation
Equating large headcount with mature capabilities
recommended_actions: Pilot a new unit/region before broad replication
Review local exceptions and decision rights; route established operations to organization journey
goals: Replicate reliably while retaining learning capacity
experiments: Operational resilience exercise with documented limits
decisions: Replicate, pause, adapt locally or withdraw
Move stable operations to established-organization review while preserving discovery for new bets
completion_criteria: Each rollout has owned outcomes, cash exposure and a review date.
next_stage_criteria: Stable execution can enter the established-organization journey; innovation can restart at discovery.
deferred: Exit/funding transaction recommendations pending jurisdiction-specific research
blocking_data: Undefined accountability or unmeasured material operating risk for a proposed rollout

classification_tree.unknown_behavior: Return candidate stages plus missing evidence; do not treat unknown as false or force a lower-stage label.
classification_tree.assignment_behavior: A supported leaf is provisional until dependencies, scope, counterevidence and context are reviewed.

if_false.action: Clarify venture scope and decision before starting stage questions.

classification_tree.source_limit: Sources support underlying search and learning concepts, not this exact tree or its classification validity.
